questions.question: In the Event Management architecture, which component polls external event tracking tools and sends event information to the ServiceNow instance?

explanation.correct: The MID Server polls external event tracking tools and maintains a connection to Event Management, sending information to your instance for storage, processing, and remediation. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/em-process-flow.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Discovery Sensors are used for Discovery probes, not event collection
ACC Agent is for Agent Client Collector, different purpose
Event Processor is not a ServiceNow component name

source.excerpt: As the computer, software, or service generates events, the MID Server polls the external event tracking tool. The MID Server, maintaining a connection to Event Management, sends the information to your instance.

questions.question: In which table does Event Management store incoming events before processing them into alerts?

explanation.correct: The instance stores events in the Event [em_event] table and attempts to generate alerts based on predefined rules and event mappings. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/em-process-flow.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: em_alert stores alerts that are generated from events
incident table stores incidents, not raw events
cmdb_ci stores configuration items, not events

source.excerpt: The instance stores events in the Event [em_event] table and attempts to generate alerts based on predefined rules and event mappings.

questions.question: Which two methods can be used to send events directly to a ServiceNow instance? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Events can be sent directly to your instance via email server, script, SNMP trap, or web service API. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/em-process-flow.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Service Catalog is for user requests, not event ingestion
Knowledge articles are informational, not event sources

source.excerpt: Events are sent directly to your instance via email server, script, SNMP trap, or web service API.

questions.question: In the Event Management process flow, what happens after Event Management generates alerts from events?

options.text: Events are immediately deleted from the system
Alert management rules are applied and alerts are prioritized for remediation
Incidents are automatically created for all alerts
MID Server restarts to process the next batch

explanation.correct: After generating alerts, Event Management applies alert management rules and prioritizes alerts for remediation and root cause analysis. This information can be viewed on dashboards, the alert list, or from a service map. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/em-architecture.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Events are retained for review regardless of alert generation
Incident creation depends on alert management rules, not automatic for all
MID Server operates continuously, not restarting per batch

source.excerpt: Event Management generates alerts, applies alert management rules, and prioritizes alerts for remediation and root cause analysis.

questions.question: For root cause analysis purposes, what does Event Management bind an alert to?

explanation.correct: For root cause analysis purposes, Event Management binds the alert to a specific Configuration Item (CI). This enables correlation with the CMDB for understanding the impact and relationships. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/em-process-flow.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Alerts are bound to CIs, not user accounts
Knowledge articles provide information, not used for alert binding
Service catalog items are for requests, not infrastructure binding

source.excerpt: For root cause analysis purposes, bind the alert to a specific Configuration Item (CI).

questions.question: Which is NOT a method for viewing Event Management alerts and information?

explanation.correct: Event Management information can be viewed on dashboards, the alert list in Alert Intelligence, or from a service map. CMDB Workspace is for configuration item management, not specifically for viewing Event Management alerts. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/em-architecture.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Dashboards display alert information and metrics
Alert Intelligence shows the alert list for remediation
Service maps show alerts in context of services

source.excerpt: This information can be viewed on dashboards, the alert list in Alert Intelligence, or from a service map.
